alternatives.argument: The local Definition states the per-observation negative derivative explicitly. ESL Algorithm 10.3 and the official Frontiers article §2.4 both describe this negative score derivative as the pseudo-residual.

The local proof composes each scalar loss with its coordinate projection, applies the published finite-dimensional total-derivative chain rule, adds the finite sum, and identifies the coordinate gradient. ESL §10.10 and Frontiers §2.4 support the score-space gradient interpretation.

ESL Algorithm 10.3 supplies the exact per-leaf line-search variant; the official Frontiers article §§2.3–2.4 independently supplies the function-space negative-gradient/base-learner approximation. The local carrier states the attained-minimizer and finite-CART conditions explicitly.

alternatives.argument: The local Definition gives the finite per-observation derivative formula explicitly. ESL Algorithm 10.3 and Natekin–Knoll §2.4 independently state the negative score derivative used as the pseudo-residual.

The local proof writes each coordinate loss as a scalar function composed with a coordinate projection, applies the published finite-dimensional chain rule, adds the finite sum, and reads off its partial-derivative vector. ESL §10.10 and Natekin–Knoll §2.4 support the score-space gradient interpretation.

The local algorithm states all inputs, attained-minimizer conditions, the finite CART residual fit, and exact leafwise line searches. ESL Algorithm 10.3 supplies this exact variant; the independent Natekin–Knoll tutorial corroborates the negative-gradient base-learner approximation. The local loss theorem proves the consequence needed from the zero-feasible offset.

For each nonempty terminal sample set the attained line minimizer has loss at most its value at the feasible zero offset. The finite CART leaves partition the training indices, so summing these inequalities proves roundwise empirical-loss nonincrease.
